truthAudit.Summary: Audited Run 2 against the visible truth set. It fully identified 14 of 20 true vulnerabilities, missed 6, and included 4 previous findings that should not be credited as confirmed true vulnerabilities. Several identified findings had severity or CWE corrections.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string injection through runtime log format
Items.Notes: The previous answer explicitly identified runtime log format being used as a printf format with controlled log_format, matching the truth anchors log_format, runtime_log_format, and printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Unbounded factorial loop and integer overflow
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the factorial loop and result *= i overflow path, matching the truth vulnerability. It underclaimed severity as Medium instead of High.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free due to memory pool cleanup before thread pool drain
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified pooled scratch pointers captured by thread-pool tasks and memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() running before tasks are guaranteed to complete.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection from configuration validator path
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified validator_cmd and config_file being concatenated and passed to system(), matching the truth anchors. It underclaimed severity as High instead of Critical.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Buffer overflow in evaluate_expression due to inverted length check
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified strcpy(input_buffer_, expression.c_str()) under an inverted length condition, matching the stack buffer overflow truth vulnerability. It overclaimed severity as Critical and used a less specific CWE.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race and lost updates in ThreadSafeCounter
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified the read of value_ before the lock and write of stale old_value inside the lock, matching the thread-pool counter race.

The previous answer identified login_attempts_ > 5, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, and authenticated_ = true, matching the logic bomb authentication vulnerability. It overclaimed severity and used an incorrect CWE.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Path traversal in admin load configuration
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified config_dir_ + filename in load_config and the admin load command path, matching the path traversal vulnerability.
The previous answer identified buffer_size_ = 256 and strcpy into expression_buffer_ from a reconstructed expression string, matching the heap overflow in the expression parser.
The previous answer explicitly identified ADMIN_SECRET with the value SC_ENT_2025_AUTH and its use in authentication.
The previous answer identified std::mt19937 with uniform_int_distribution bounded to 1000 through 9999 for session tokens, matching the weak PRNG vulnerability. It underclaimed severity and CWE.
The previous answer did not identify the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time / localtime update in log_debug_message.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection in emergency audit event logging
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified TEMP/TMPDIR-controlled supercalc_emergency.log path being used in a system() command. It framed this as command injection, but the underlying insecure temporary file handling was present in the previous output.

The previous answer did not identify persistent authentication state as a vulnerability. It discussed the emergency override but did not report authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ persistence as the issue.
The previous answer did not identify the unhandled std::stod(tokens[3]) exception path in handle_variable_command. Its substr out_of_range finding is a different latent exception-handling issue.
The previous answer did not identify the integer underflow in memory-pool block split involving previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES and fragment.size = remaining.
The previous answer did not identify unbounded recursion through parse_expression, parse_term, and parse_factor with PAREN_OPEN.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Data race on expression result cache
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified result_cache_ being read and written without using cache_mutex_ in evaluate_cached(), matching the result-cache data race. It overclaimed severity as High instead of Medium.
The previous answer did not identify the TOCTOU race in load_config between std::filesystem::exists, sleep_for, and std::ifstream.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Division by zero in route scoring
Items.Notes: The previous answer identified 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length) with empty input causing division by zero. It overclaimed severity as Medium instead of Low.
